questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from the lane next to the solid yellow line.
You cannot pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross it to pass. The broken line is on your side if you are allowed to pass.

questions.question: If dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, what should you turn on?
questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly. This helps other drivers see you too.

questions.question: When turning left from a one-way street with multiple lanes, which lane should you start from?

options.text: The lane closest to the left curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the leftmost lane of a one-way street.

questions.question: What do yellow lines separate on the road?

options.text: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of two-way roads. Solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass. Broken yellow lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: How can you help keep the car behind you at a safe distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Driving at a steady speed helps the driver behind you stay a safe distance away. Also signal before you turn, change lanes, or slow down.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign shows that a divided highway is starting. Stay to the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop if needed.
Come to a full stop, then go when safe.
Proceed carefully, you do not always have to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop at the stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk or intersection so you can see any oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are on your left and parked vehicles are on your right. Where should you steer?

options.text: Down the middle between both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Down the middle between both sides.
questions.explanation: Steer a middle course between the oncoming cars and the parked cars.

questions.question: Pedestrians are jaywalking across the street. What must you do?

options.text: You do not have to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop for them.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: When bad weather or low light requires you to use your lights, which should you use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect light back at you, creating glare and making it harder to see.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder. Look for other drivers trying to move into the same lane. Never change lanes or pass in an intersection.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. To prevent it in rain, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Move to the shoulder as soon as rain starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: In rain, slow down to avoid hydroplaning. Driving too fast can cause your tires to float on water and lose grip with the road. This makes your vehicle very hard to control.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off water and precipitation back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake hard and fast to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Apply brakes gently with increasing pressure so your vehicle stops smoothly.

questions.question: You should drive on the shoulder to pass a car:

options.text: If the car ahead is turning left.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you to be there and may pull off the road onto the shoulder.

questions.question: What should you do if an emergency vehicle has flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Pull over to the side and stop completely.
Keep driving but try to stay out of the way.
Try to reach your destination before it catches up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side and stop completely.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, pull to the right side of the road and stop completely. Do not try to drive away from it.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that stop at all railroad crossings (school buses, trucks with hazardous materials).

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both of the above.
questions.explanation: Be very careful at railroad crossings. Only cross when you know no train is coming from either direction. Watch for school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials, which must stop at all railroad crossings.

questions.question: In a roundabout, drivers should:

options.text: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
Yield to traffic entering the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: In a roundabout, traffic flows counterclockwise around a center island. When you enter, yield to traffic already inside. Follow the circle to the right and exit onto your street.

questions.question: Driving slower than other traffic is:

options.text: A good idea in bad weather.
Okay if you don't know the speed limit.
Often dangerous because drivers may get frustrated and try to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often dangerous because drivers may get frustrated and try to pass.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than other traffic can be hazardous. Impatient drivers behind you may take dangerous risks to pass you.

questions.question: The right way to make a right turn is to:

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the centerline before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach in the right lane, then move toward the middle before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, signal to warn other drivers. Slow down and stay as close as possible to the right curb as you approach the intersection.

questions.question: When is your reaction time slower?
questions.correctAnswerText: After drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your ability to see clearly and makes you less alert. As you drink more, your judgment gets worse and your driving skills decrease. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and other vehicles.

questions.question: Which statement is true about medicines and driving?

options.text: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medicines are safe for driving if you take the recommended dose.
Any medicine prescribed by a doctor is safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medicines—whether prescription or over-the-counter—can be dangerous and may affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy and impair your driving. You are responsible for knowing how your medicines affect your ability to drive.

questions.question: What does a red curb mean?

options.text: You can pick up or drop off passengers here.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red-painted curb.

questions.question: What should a driver do?

options.text: Focus only on the middle of the road.
Watch to the sides, ahead, and behind your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch to the sides, ahead, and behind your car.
questions.explanation: You should watch all around your vehicle—to the sides, ahead, and behind. Good drivers know what is happening everywhere around them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. Do not make a right turn at an intersection with this sign.

questions.question: When traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to have an accident if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within that speed range.
questions.explanation: Match your speed to the other traffic (as long as they are following speed limits). Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot crash into each other. Most crashes happen when some vehicles drive faster or slower than others.

questions.question: How should you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Look over your left or right shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the correct shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be careful.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, look both ways, and go carefully.

questions.question: If you are being passed on the right and left while driving in the center lane of an expressway, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: On a road with four or more lanes, drive in the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. If you are driving slower than traffic on an interstate, use the right lane.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead has red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Stop until the lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: The flashing red lights and stop arm on a school bus activate when students are getting on or off. Do not move until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes back. Never pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off students.
